title: Pesarattu
steps: Soak green gram for 3–4 hours. Grind with ginger, green chilli, cumin and salt into a slightly coarse batter (no fermentation needed).
Heat a tawa, pour and spread the batter into a thin crepe. Drizzle oil and cook both sides till crisp.
Serve hot with allam (ginger) pachadi or coconut chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Signature Andhra breakfast crepe – lighter and more protein-rich than regular dosa.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh and crisp.

title: Rava Upma (Uppindi)
steps: Dry-roast the rava lightly. Temper mustard, dals, curry leaves, chilli and onion in oil/ghee.
Add water (and vegetables if using), bring to a boil, then add the roasted rava while stirring.
Cook till soft and fluffy. Serve with chutney or pickle.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves
Mustard, cumin, urad dal, chana dal

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday Andhra tiffin – made with rava.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A little ghee elevates the flavour.

title: Broken Rice Upma (Uppindi)
steps: Dry-roast the broken rice lightly. Temper mustard, dals, curry leaves, chilli and onion in oil/ghee.
Add water (and vegetables if using), bring to a boil, then add the roasted broken rice while stirring.
Cook till soft and fluffy. Serve with chutney or pickle.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves
Mustard, cumin, urad dal, chana dal

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday Andhra tiffin – made with broken rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A little ghee elevates the flavour.

title: Idli with Sambar & Chutney
steps: Steam fermented idli batter in moulds till soft and fluffy.
Prepare a tangy Andhra-style sambar with tamarind, vegetables and sambar powder.
Serve hot idlis with sambar and chutney, often with a sprinkle of karapodi (gunpowder).

fullIngredients.name: Toor dal, vegetables (pumpkin, brinjal, drumstick), tamarind, sambar powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Staple South Indian breakfast adapted to Andhra tastes with spicier sambar and podi.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Soft idlis are essential.

title: Pulihora (Tamarind Rice)
steps: Prepare a thick tamarind paste cooked with turmeric and salt.
Temper mustard, curry leaves, chillies, peanuts and hing in oil. Mix into the tamarind.
Gently mix the tempered tamarind into cooled cooked rice so every grain is coated.
Rest for a while for flavours to develop. Serve at room temperature.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard, curry leaves, dry red chilli, peanuts, turmeric, hing

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Temple-style tamarind rice – tangy, spicy and aromatic.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A little jaggery balances the sourness.

title: Gongura Pachadi
steps: Wash and roughly chop gongura leaves. Cook or sauté till soft and the sourness mellows.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic and red chilli in oil. Grind or mash the leaves with the tempering and salt into a coarse chutney.
Serve with rice and ghee or as a side.

fullIngredients.name: Garlic, dry red chilli, mustard, cumin

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Andhra relish – intensely sour and spicy.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The signature flavour of the state.

title: Tomato Pappu (Andhra Dal)
steps: Pressure-cook toor dal with turmeric and tomato till soft. Mash lightly.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic, chilli and curry leaves in oil/ghee and pour over the dal.
Serve thick and creamy with rice and ghee.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard, cumin, dry red chilli, curry leaves for tempering

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Andhra tomato dal - thick and robust.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Perfect comfort food with rice.

title: Gongura Pappu (Andhra Dal with Sorrel)
steps: Pressure-cook toor dal with turmeric and gongura leaves till soft. Mash lightly.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic, chilli and curry leaves in oil/ghee and pour over the dal.
Serve thick and creamy with rice and ghee.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard, cumin, dry red chilli, curry leaves for tempering

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Andhra gongura dal - tangy and robust.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The sourness of gongura perfectly complements the dal.

title: Natu Kodi Pulusu (Country Chicken Curry)
steps: Marinate chicken with turmeric and salt. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and chilli till golden.
Add tomato, spice powders and tamarind extract. Cook till oil separates.
Add chicken and simmer till tender and the gravy is thick and spicy.
Serve with rice or ragi sangati.

fullIngredients.name: Tamarind, red chilli powder, coriander, garam masala

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Fiery Andhra country-chicken curry – tamarind and Guntur chilli define the flavour.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Slow cooking brings out the best taste.

title: Chepala Pulusu (Fish Curry)
steps: Lightly fry fish pieces. Prepare a tamarind-based gravy with onion, tomato, garlic and chilli powder.
Temper mustard, fenugreek and curry leaves. Add the gravy and fish. Simmer gently.
Serve with steamed rice.

fullIngredients.name: Tamarind, onion, tomato, garlic, red chilli

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic coastal Andhra fish curry – tangy, spicy and aromatic.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Do not overcook the fish.

title: Mirchi Bajji
steps: Slit and deseed chillies if desired. Make a thick besan batter with spices and ginger-garlic paste.
Dip each chilli in the batter and deep-fry till golden and crisp.
Serve hot with onion, chutney or as is.

fullIngredients.name: Besan, rice flour, chilli powder, ajwain, ginger-garlic paste, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Andhra street snack – spicy, crunchy and addictive.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten immediately.

title: Punugulu
steps: Mix chopped onion, chilli, curry leaves and cumin into the fermented batter.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry till golden and crisp outside, soft inside.
Serve with coconut or peanut chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, cumin

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Andhra-style deep-fried dumplings from leftover or fresh batter.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Crispy and perfect with evening tea.

title: Gutti Vankaya Kura (Stuffed Brinjal Curry)
steps: Slit brinjals crosswise without cutting through. Stuff with a roasted peanut-sesame-coconut-spice mixture.
Cook in a tamarind-onion-garlic gravy till the brinjals are soft and the masala coats them.
Serve with rice or roti.

fullIngredients.name: Peanuts, sesame, coconut, spices for stuffing
Onion, tamarind, garlic, chilli powder, oil

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Stuffed brinjal curry – a festive and everyday favourite.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The stuffing should be well-roasted for depth of flavour.

title: Gongura Mamsam (Mutton with Gongura)
steps: Cook mutton with onion, ginger-garlic and spices till tender.
Separately cook gongura leaves till soft, then mash or blend.
Combine the gongura with the mutton and simmer till the flavours marry and the gravy thickens.
Serve with rice or roti.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Andhra mutton dish where the sourness of gongura balances the richness of the meat.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: One of the most celebrated non-veg preparations of the state.
